headline: Accellera forms the UVM-AMS Working Group to standardize mixed-signal UVM extensions
fact: Accellera formed the UVM-AMS Working Group on November 19, 2019 after a proposed-working-group phase that began with a May 2019 meeting in Munich, naming Patrick Lynch as chair. The charter targeted a unified UVM-based analog/mixed-signal verification methodology, including standardized driving and monitoring of mixed-signal nets, stimulus, scoreboarding and analysis, plus a framework for reusable analog/mixed-signal verification components derived from digital-centric verification IP. Accellera said the planned standard was intended to support ready-to-use analog/mixed-signal verification IP from tool and IP providers.

sources.title: UVM-AMS Working Group Formed to Standardize UVM Analog/Mixed-Signal Extensions
sources.summary: Accellera's November 19, 2019 announcement names Patrick Lynch as UVM-AMS Working Group chair, defines the charter, describes its May 2019 proposed-working-group precursor, and states the goal of reusable AMS verification components and ready-to-use AMS verification IP.

sources.title: UVM-AMS: a UVM-Based Analog Verification Standard
sources.summary: The official DVCon U.S. 2021 workshop record identifies Patrick Lynch of Xilinx among the key Accellera UVM-AMS Working Group members, corroborating the public identity linked to the 2019 chair role.
